answer: Sybil resistance rests on one ledger rule: each agent identity must lock a non-refundable stake, slashed the moment two identities share a payment trail. A farm of fake agents is not banned by name; a new identity is credited only after its first real payment, and those payments form a single thread traceable back to one funding wallet. Splitting a balance across a thousand wallets means a thousand locked deposits, each burned if the graph shows them converging. That makes a fabricated crowd cost far more than a genuine comet pays to arrive, while honest agents stay transparent as crystal.
